items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I heard Nat King Cole on these big records

ctx.x: No kidding. Did you get to play at all?

Oh yeah, we did play a lot. So we listened to a lot of V-discs in those days, all the best records. I heard Nat King Cole on these big records, you know they had these large 15 minute transcriptions, with a big long arm and they would play them and they’d last 15 minutes.
15 minutes. You know now that seems like nothing. It’s like such an annoyance with the LPs now, you have to turn them over.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Well Nat Cole put it together, and everybody used it.

ctx.x: Well Nat Cole put it together, and everybody used it. Art Tatum had the same thing and I mean he did it because they get more money as opposed to playing solo piano. They told him put Tiny Grimes in and Slam Stewart and according to Tiny, he never told him what tune he was playing. They were just there and Art’s making big money and never said anything. In fact the funny line was that Tiny said, “It was a great honor but it really wasn’t a great pleasure,” or something like that.
Yeah? He didn’t even tell them what tune he was going to play.
